# Historical experiment results and frozen TEST reevaluation

Updated 2026-11-17T22:13:46.883018+01:00. **Frozen evaluation is finished.** Unavailable checkpoints/source and non-detector experiments remain explicitly qualified.

The PoseFlow table contains **117 run/variant/pilot/objective-phase rows**, across **55 version families** plus the unnumbered codebook branches. This is distinct from **351 raw source records** covering the wider repository history. Failed duplicate starts and proven resumed phases are linked inside their experiment; independent fresh attempts and genuinely different controls remain separate. Earlier architectures, sweeps, codecs, conditional pilots and evaluation-only history have their own tables below.

All39 strictly reusable historical conditions reproduce their original AP and configuration hashes.

Comparison AP columns use a 0–100 scale. Markdown rounds AP to two decimals; CSV/JSON comparison fields retain full numeric precision. Labelled raw archival payloads retain their original source scales. Full TEST means all 8,000 official TEST images; fixed32 TEST is reported separately. Unknown does not mean zero. N/A means the experiment does not produce that measurement. Source, selected checkpoint, resize, seed, precision, sampler, confidence and NMS contracts are attached to each evaluation. Evaluation elapsed time includes postprocessing and metric aggregation and is not a controlled inference-speed benchmark.

† For RTMPose and upstream-pose refiners, bbox AP belongs to the unchanged published detector proposals; these models have no box head. Pose-only models without such a pipeline box measurement show bbox N/A.

The original ED-Pose asset is treated as TRAIN+VAL pretrained. Recent VAL results remain historical diagnostics and never fill TEST columns. Historical TEST monitoring/model selection makes TEST a development benchmark. Different resolution, budget, decoder and postprocessing settings limit direct comparisons.

Historical reuse requires the archived model definition as well as evaluator/coverage/checkpoint evidence. Evaluator/importer-only pins are insufficient; their original TEST numbers remain in a separate source-unverified history table. [Verification policy correction](</home/gasparyanartur/dev/pose-graph-diff/results/all_run_audit/20261116_203800/verification_policy_correction.json>).

Checkpoint epoch numbers retain the source framework convention; completed training budget is reported separately from the age of the selected checkpoint. Checkpoint selection is frozen before evaluation: retain documented historical best/final rules, or use the latest saved valid endpoint of unfinished training. No retraining or TEST checkpoint/hyperparameter sweep occurs. V35–V41 are box-only; their AP is bbox AP and pose AP is N/A. Conditional/GT-assisted or codec measurements never fill detector AP columns.

Verified historical TEST conditions: **39**. Newly completed full TEST evaluations: **200**. The coordinators target five concurrent GPU evaluations with a 4 GiB admission budget per evaluator. [Historical verification](</home/gasparyanartur/dev/pose-graph-diff/results/all_run_audit/20261116_203800/historical_test_verification.json>); [shared fixed32 manifest](</home/gasparyanartur/dev/pose-graph-diff/results/all_run_audit/20261116_203800/fixed32_test.json>). All original artifacts are preserved.

A logical row can contain several launch/continuation records. The exact phase statuses, budgets, original paths, checkpoint results and config differences remain in the reconciliation JSON and raw appendix. Evaluation-only records are supporting evidence rather than independent trained models.

The original ED-Pose and released DiffusionRegPose references each distinguish 256/427 and 800/1333 protocols using the same respective weights. These are evaluation protocols, not separate training runs or model versions. ## Conclusions and limits

The native grouped ED-Pose reference measures **51.87 pose AP / 46.44 bbox AP** on full TEST at 256/427. Its separate fixed32 TEST result is 45.33 / 40.78. This reduced-resolution reference differs from the original 800/1333 protocol.

Recent VAL improvements survive as optimization diagnostics under pretrained overlap. Image-only TEST conclusions are restricted to the independently recorded frozen evaluations. Clean codec fidelity, conditional transfer and exact weight restoration do not establish native detector quality. Partial runs cannot establish a matched full-budget architectural gain.

The same original ED-Pose checkpoint at 800/1333 measures **70.26 pose AP / 60.59 bbox AP** on full TEST, and 65.00 / 60.20 on common fixed32 TEST. This supplies the native reference for paper-resolution runs using identical released weights.

The fixed released DiffusionRegPose asset at 800/1333, [Released pretrained DiffusionRegPose R50 / native DDIM /800x1333 reference protocol](<#experiment-drp_released_800>), measures 72.82 pose AP / 63.08 bbox AP. It is a separately pinned native frozen replay, not a relabelling of the older source-unverified paper-scale measurement. Reduced-resolution references and models with different proposal, decoder or NMS contracts remain qualified separately.

The matched V9 skeleton-bias intervention, [V9](<#experiment-run_215>) versus [V5](<#experiment-run_203>), changes full TEST pose/bbox by -0.20/-0.13 AP points at the declared final K3 endpoints after 80 epochs. This is a single-seed comparison; successful bias gradients and bias0 parity alone do not establish a detector gain.

The matched residual-h comparison after 80 epochs, [V24 matched / h enabled](<#experiment-run_147>) versus [V24 matched / no h control](<#experiment-run_146>), improves full TEST pose/bbox by +0.38/+0.18 AP points in one training seed, with added compute. This is bounded support for this specific intervention. The common fixed32 subset ranks these arms in the opposite order; a small subset cannot replace full-set evaluation.

The original reduced-model matching control, [diffusionregpose development compatible 256 keep layers ota](<#experiment-run_050>) versus [diffusionregpose development compatible 256 keep layers](<#experiment-run_049>), changes full TEST pose/bbox by +3.16/+0.99 AP points at matched final endpoints after 80 epochs. Assignment and positive-count normalization are the intervention; this one-seed result does not establish a paper-scale advantage.

The verified [V42 jepa](<#experiment-run_252>) control does not improve pose AP over image-confidence V42 at K1/K4/K8. [V45 task pose / JEPA](<#experiment-run_264>) improves the matched multi-call endpoint while losing one-call pose AP; K4 still trails K1. These results support recipe-specific conclusions about generated-state use, rather than a general rejection or validation of JEPA.

[V44 rollout / rollout](<#experiment-run_260>) improves the preselected K4 endpoint over its forward-corruption control, but this replay does not certify the original one-call-preservation and conditional trajectory gates. The velocity endpoint, [V44 parameterization / v](<#experiment-run_257>), has negligible detector pose AP; unequal selected ages limit a parameterization-only causal claim. Original conditional/VAL evidence remains separately labelled.

The six latent-generation recipes V26, V28 and V31–V34 completed 80 epochs and have 0.77–7.95 pose AP at their declared Gaussian-start conditions. Clean code reconstruction and memorization of four images do not establish competitive image-only generation. The separate codec/conditional tables explain capability and failure scope; this evidence does not reject learned representations generally.

[V43 frozen vae](<#experiment-run_285>) completes 80 epochs with 19.39 pose AP / 38.08 bbox AP at native K4. A fixed codec fixes the mapping from geometry to target codes, but there is no matched moving-code pose control that isolates the value of freezing. Its clean-code/conditional results and the low AP of earlier latent recipes therefore cannot establish a general latent-representation conclusion.
